The half-life of facts is the time it takes for half of what a field holds to
be superseded or shown to be untrue. A quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP)
model of the immune system can be no more certain than the biology written
into it, so the half-life of immunology facts, or the spread in what
immunologists believe, bounds how far such a model can be trusted. This
project asks whether AI can measure either one, starting with how B cell
subsets are defined by their surface markers.

## Documents

- [Working specification](specification.qmd). The question, the B cell
  immunophenotype starting point, how AI could do the measuring, and the
  steps.
- [Toward a survey of immunologists to support QSP model development](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cC56NsD-lwQEeJK78XGLqNEyyO51PZ0MZx6NLKl2G4U/edit)
  (Google Doc, from 2024). The earlier idea: a short survey of immunologists
  on immuno-oncology biology, the reasons for and against doing it, and a
  draft of the survey questions. Thoughts from it are still to be folded in
  here.
